traceability.evidence: 1) Implementation: The JSDoc/annotation parsing logic is in src/rules/helpers/valid-annotation-format-internal.ts and src/rules/valid-annotation-format.ts. normalizeCommentLine only detects @story, @req, and @supports (regex /@story\b|@req\b|@supports\b/) and otherwise strips a leading '*' but returns the rest of the line unchanged. processCommentLine treats any non-empty line when a PendingAnnotation exists as a continuation, appending normalized.trim() to the current annotation value. There is no generic JSDoc tag boundary detection (no /^\s*\*?\s*@\w+/ helper) and no special handling for other JSDoc tags like @param or @returns. As a result, for the example in the story: `/** * @req REQ-OPTIMIZATION * @param {object} data */`, line 1 starts a pending @req with value 'REQ-OPTIMIZATION', and line 2 ('@param {object} data' after normalization) is appended as continuation, yielding a combined value that will be collapsed to 'REQ-OPTIMIZATION@param{object}data'—exactly the broken behavior described in the story. 2) Tests: The valid-annotation-format tests in tests/rules/valid-annotation-format.test.ts cover multi-line values and a JSDoc-style comment with leading stars but only for traceability tags themselves (e.g., @story and @req); there are no tests where @story/@req/@supports coexist with @param, @returns, @throws, or any other JSDoc tags. There is no test file named tests/unit/annotation-parser.test.ts as referenced in the story, and no tests mention docs/stories/022.0-DEV-JSDOC-COEXISTENCE.story.md or its REQ-JSDOC-* requirements. 3) Documentation: docs/rules/valid-annotation-format.md still documents behavior as concatenating all lines that belong to the same annotation and removing internal whitespace (including newlines); it does not mention JSDoc tag boundaries, generic @tag detection, or provide examples mixing traceability annotations with other JSDoc tags in different positions. 4) Search: A repository-wide search shows no implementation or tests referencing 022.0-DEV-JSDOC-COEXISTENCE, and no helper that recognizes arbitrary JSDoc tags as boundaries.
traceability.notes: The behavior required by docs/stories/022.0-DEV-JSDOC-COEXISTENCE.story.md has not been fully implemented. The current parser still treats any non-empty line in a block comment as a continuation of the current @story/@req annotation value when a pending annotation exists, regardless of whether that line begins with another JSDoc tag like @param or @returns. There is no generic JSDoc-tag boundary detection to terminate annotation values when a new @tag appears, so the specific bug described in the story (e.g., REQ-OPTIMIZATION@param{object}data) still exists. Tests do not cover coexistence scenarios with other JSDoc tags, and the documentation has not been updated with examples or explanation for JSDoc coexistence. Therefore multiple acceptance criteria (Before Other Tags, After Other Tags, Mixed Positions, Proper Termination, JSDoc Tag Detection, Continuation Lines, Error Messages tuned to avoid these false positives, Documentation, and Tests) are not satisfied, so the story is failed.
